extracted.intended_audience: new and existing patent examiners, assistant examiners, and DIP administrative staff (Department of Intellectual Property, Thailand)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and internal standards for recruiting, training, evaluating, and measuring performance of patent examiners and related patent office processes (timeliness, examination quality, IT/tools, and backlog reduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Business knowledge (understanding of laws and examination guideline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understands the Section 3 (definitions); Understands the Section 9 (non-patentable inventions); Understands the Section 10, 11, 14, 15 and 16 (rights); Understands the Section 17 (making of applications); Understands the Section 19 (priority); Understands the Section (amendments); Understands the Section 23 (secrecy order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as items in the Basic abilities check sheet for assistant examiners; expected to be demonstrated in annual review and used as a basis for training and promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding of contents of description
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct understanding of the contents; Accurately comprehend and evaluate the technical features and aspects of the claimed invention in the light of the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated in on-the-job training check sheet; necessary for effective prior art assessment and claim analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search skills (domestic and foreign prior art search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a basic search for domestic documents; Conduct a basic search for foreign documents; Comprehend the technical aspects of the claimed invention and conduct an accurate and effective prior art search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training includes use of searching tools, public web (WIPO, EPO, USPTO, JPO) and cooperation work sharing tools (e.g., JPO AIPN). Search skill proficiency is part of the Basic abilities check sheet and promotion criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is an explicit topic in the Patent Examination curriculum and examination guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taught in the 2-week Patent Examination module (overview of Patent Examination, Examination guidelines, Novelty). Examiners should be able to identify novelty-relevant features in descriptions/claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventive step is a main topic in the Patent Examination curriculum (listed under Inventive step).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered in training modules and examination guidelines; examiners must assess whether claimed subject matter involves an inventive step relative to prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Classification is a topic in the Patent Examination curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must classify applications appropriately as part of search and examination workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for description
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for description are an explicit curriculum topic: what the description must contain to support claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered in classroom and on-the-job training; used to evaluate sufficiency of disclosure and written-description compliance during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for claims are an explicit curriculum topic: what constitutes acceptable claim drafting and scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners trained to assess clarity, support, and scope of claims and to propose/amend claims when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment (claim amendment procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment is a listed topic in the Patent Examination curriculum and in work instructions (amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must know the legal and procedural rules for amendments (during prosecution, opposition, appeal) and apply them consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilization of Examination Results of Other IP Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilization of Examination Results of Other IP Offices is part of the Patent Examination curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training emphasizes using foreign office results (WIPO, JPO, EPO, USPTO) to inform examination and improve consistency and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination guidelines coverage (scope of chapters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination guideline for invention patent and petty patent includes: Chapter 1 examination for Invention patent; Chapter 2 opposition; Chapter 3 examination for petty patent; Chapter 4 international application examination (PCT); Chapter 5 examination for chemistry and pharmaceutical fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must be familiar with the full guideline and its chapter-specific procedures, especially for specialized fields (chemistry/pharmaceuticals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Manual and Tools proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Manual; Patent Search; Work Flow; E-Patent; Work Instruction (by group) including Ordinary Examination, E-Patent (by group), Workshop, Patent Act (opposition article), Patent Act (appeal article).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should be competent in using the patent manual, e-patent system (in-house), and group-specific work instructions to perform examinations and administrative tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-the-job training (Phase 1 and 2) and promotion roadmap
rubrics_metrics.description: On the job training (Phase 1); Training examiner part 1; On the job training (Phase 2); Training examiner part 2; Promoted to an Examiner with full discretion (3-6th year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured multi-phase on-the-job training with specified duration and milestones; promotion contingent on demonstrated competencies over 3–6 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-the-job training (classroom lecture) content and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Off-the-Job training (Classroom lecture) covering introductory issues, IP laws and registration process, IP international cooperation, IT system, and patent examination topics with specified week allocations (e.g., 1 week topics, 2 weeks Patent Examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classroom modules delivered by DIP staff, external specialists, and partner offices (JPO, WIPO, KIPO, EPO, USPTO) form part of certification for assistant examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-Site Training objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The training purpose for assistant examiners is intended to taste and understand the invention courses and production system, learn technology trends, ultimately improve the exact and effective examination works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical exposure to industry and production systems to ground examiners in real-world technology contexts; part of comprehensive training.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-to-One Guidance Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistant examiners will receive the one-to-one training from supervisor or an experienced patent examiner to receive instructions and gain experience in all aspects of patent law and develop the skills required by an examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentorship model: individualized instruction covering law, procedure, and practical examination skills; important for accelerating competency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group study Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of group study the same specific case and learn how to analyze the invention and how to deal with the examination procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer-learning focused on case analysis improves consistency and shared understanding of examination standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation for On-the-Job training (Basic abilities check sheet & annual review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic abilities check sheet (3-year promotion version) including Self-evaluation (by Assistant examiner), Rating by Supervisor, Menu for improvement (Full-in for the items × or D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal annual review process with documented sign-off (Approved by Director, Checked by Supervising) used to track development, identify improvement needs, and support promotion decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training assessment items (search, technical comprehension, legal knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items include business knowledge (law sections), search (understanding description contents, search skills), comprehension and evaluation of technical features relative to state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on integrated technical-legal skills required for competent examination; criteria are tested via check sheets and supervised evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment qualifications and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify qualifications as required technical fields; Announcement of job application (pass criteria of civil servant test); Pass the written examination; Pass the interview; Fill the post; Probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruitment emphasizes domain-specific technical qualifications (Ph.D./Master distribution by group), formal civil service testing, and multi-stage selection with probationary period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing targets and manpower planning
rubrics_metrics.description: 3 years plan to recruit more government officials with detailed yearly increases for trademark registrars, invention patent examiners, design patent examiners, petty patent, trademark appeal legal officers, patent appeal legal officers, law cases legal officers, IT positions; total targets (e.g., 120 as of Sep.2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative staffing goals tied to backlog reduction and improved timeliness; used for budgeting and recruitment priority-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely protection / Backlog KPIs and targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Current backlog figures and targets: reduce time frame from receipt of application to publication from 20 months to 12 months; reduce substantive examination process from 36 months to 12 months; Petty Patent current 11 months -> target register within 6 months; Industrial design current 3 years -> target register within 12 months; Trademark current 12–15 months -> target register within 6 months (without opposition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit timeliness targets form the core performance metrics for the patent office; progress monitored via implementation plans and staffing/IT changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation plan for backlog resolution (system & development phases)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1st Phase: Change system hardware to enable a faster system and to support new legal instruments (e.g., Sound, time) as well as the Madrid Protocol. 2nd Phase: System development using new technology to improve trademark registration management system (different from the 1st phase which changes hardware but uses old technology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-phased IT modernization approach: immediate hardware upgrades followed by software/system redevelopment; tied to supporting new treaties and improving capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve IP registration system: e-filing and e-patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent e-filing - launched on 3 May 2015; Trademark e-filing - launched on 3 May 2016; Improvement efficiency through work flow diagnosis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-filing adoption is a key operational criterion to reduce processing time and increase efficiency; examiners must be trained on e-patent systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation and further training with other patent offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in training course with other patent offices (cooperation among ASEAN such as JPO, EPO, IP Australia, SIPO and other); WIPO, JPO, KIPO, EPO, USPTO involvement; WIPO national case Training for Global Patent; AIPN cooperation work sharing tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-office cooperation and external courses recommended to raise examiner skill levels, provide exposure to international best practices, and enable work-sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for specialized fields (chemistry & pharmaceutical, biotechnology, engineering, electronics etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Examination includes Chapters/Modules addressing chemistry and pharmaceutical fields; curriculum lists groups (Engineering, Electrical and IC, Physics, Petrochemicals, Technology Chemistry, Pharmaceutical, Biotechnology, etc.) with Ph.D./Master targets for recruitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized subject-matter training and recruitment targets are required to ensure examiners have adequate technical expertise for complex fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and establishment of examination quality controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenges include establishing a training system for all examiners; to make an examiner having a high capability; increase efficiency of examination; to reduce a backlog; establishing the monitoring system for patent examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office-level obligations include creating a monitoring system, quality controls, standardized training, and measurable improvement plans to address long delays and quality/consistency issues.
